concept.title: Preface / Notice / Copyright
concept.abstract: This section covers the Preface, Notice, and Copyright sections in DOCX — their role as front matter that applies to the whole document rather than a single chapter — and one scenario: a Copyright Notice section correctly identified and routed to the bookmap. The converter matches heading text against a list of recognized front matter keywords and maps a match to <frontmatter>; a heading without an exact match is still evaluated as a front matter candidate when it appears before the first chapter.

conbody.p: Preface, Notice, and Copyright sections carry legal statements, ownership information, and introductory content that apply to the whole document, not just one chapter.

These sections are identified by their heading text — "Copyright Notice," "Preface," or "Legal Notice" — placed before the first numbered chapter. Each one must use the Heading 1 style. This is required because the converter relies on heading text to tell front matter apart from chapter content, and regulatory or audit reviews expect this content in a fixed, predictable location.

In a .docx file, a front matter section is authored the same way as a chapter: a Heading 1 paragraph followed by body content. It is positioned before the first substantive chapter rather than within the chapter sequence.

The converter matches each Heading 1 text against a list of recognised front matter keywords and routes a match to <frontmatter> in the bookmap. It also applies content pattern recognition to sections without an exact keyword match: a Heading 1 section appearing before the first chapter is still a front matter candidate if its content is consistent with preliminary material.
